sources.citation: Bernhardt, Julia. 2019. A comparative study of the Northern Naga languages and their genetic classification. CanIL Electronic Working Papers 5: 1-23.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Lexicostatistic comparison of 15 wordlists (462 items, LSDO data) from seven Myanmar Northern Naga languages including one Lao [nlq] list; p. 13: 'The focus was limited to lexical similarity based on segmental phonology, excluding morphosyntactic and other phonological features, such as tone and syllable structure.' Lao is 62% similar to Chen-Kayu (p. 18). Only general remark: 'Naga languages tend to be tonal, isolating, and have SOV constituent order (Marrison 1967)' (p. 4).
